question: Does redesigning the 12-state hash-routed SPA to 0% deterministic strata (all CANDIDATES lists contain only distinct next states, ensuring every (current, action) pair is stochastic) eliminate the per-stratum plug-in PMI null bias that persists at +0.742 bits for small strata under the shuffled-action null — and does this redesign enable a valid beyond-Markov K3-K2 test, or is the bias intrinsic to plug-in estimation regardless of determinism ratio?
hypothesis: H0 (null): The per-stratum plug-in PMI null bias persists at |null_mean| >= 0.1 bits even when all strata are stochastic (0% deterministic). This means the bias is intrinsic to the plug-in estimator's behavior across strata of varying size, not caused by deterministic/stochastic mixing. H1 (alternative): At least one estimator from {weighted-PMI, KNN-CMI} achieves |null_mean| < 0.1 bits on the fully-stochastic SPA, indicating the bias was partially or fully caused by deterministic strata. H2 (beyond-Markov, conditional on H1 passing): K3 PMI - K2 PMI > 0.1 bits with bootstrap 95% CI lower > 0.0 at N=5000 on the fully-stochastic SPA.
falsifier: C1 (null control): All estimators have |shuffled-action null mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000 on the fully-stochastic SPA (bias persists despite removing all deterministic strata). C2 (beyond-Markov, conditional on H1): K3-K2 <= 0.1 bits OR bootstrap CI includes zero. C3 (positive control): K3 PMI < 1.0 bit OR permutation p > 0.001 on the 8-state deterministic SPA. C4 (convergence): K2(N=50000) - K2(N=5000) > 0.2 bits for any estimator passing C1 (asymptotic non-convergence persists).

baselines.description: Weighted-averaged per-stratum Laplace-smoothed conditional PMI (the parent's primary estimator, null_mean=0.407 on parent SPA)
KNN CMI estimator (k=5, alpha=1.0, kNN distance-weighted Laplace, null_mean=-0.262 on parent SPA)
baselines.expected: null_mean may shift sign or magnitude relative to parent due to removed deterministic strata

baselines.description: Equal-weight per-stratum PMI (parent null_mean=0.704, worsened bias from up-weighting small strata)
baselines.expected: null_mean >= 0.1 (bias likely persists; included for completeness)

baselines.description: Per-stratum bias decomposition into size buckets (5-9, 10-19, 20-49) to test whether bias becomes uniform across sizes when deterministic strata removed
baselines.expected: If bias is deterministic-caused: all buckets converge toward 0. If intrinsic: small strata still carry higher bias (+0.742 region)

positive_control: 8-state fully deterministic SPA (same as parent C3). Every (state, action) maps to a single next state via hash. K3 PMI should be >= 1.0 bit with p <= 0.001. This validates the estimator pipeline on a known-deterministic environment before testing on the stochastic target.
null_control: Shuffled-action null: for each of 500 permutations, shuffle action labels within each session (preserving session structure and url_before url_after pairing), recompute per-stratum PMI, take weighted mean across strata. The null mean must satisfy |mean| < 0.1 bits for any estimator to pass C1. Unit of permutation is action-label within session (same as parent).
measurement_validity: SPA redesign is implemented by modifying CANDIDATES so every (state, action) list contains N>=2 distinct next states (no duplicates, no self-loops as sole candidate). The hash function selects one of the N candidates. This guarantees every stratum has H(S_next | state, action) > 0.
The determinism check: for every (state, action) pair, |unique(CANDIDATES[state][action])| >= 2. If any pair fails, the experiment is MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
N=5000 transitions (50 sessions x 100 steps) with seed=42, same collection procedure as parent.
Strata with < 5 records are skipped (MIN_STRATUM_SIZE=5, same as parent). Descriptive reporting of stratum size distribution.
All estimators use the same Laplace smoothing alpha=1.0 as parent for comparability.
Bootstrap CI uses 200 trajectory-block resamples (same as parent).
Bonferroni correction for 2 primary comparisons (weighted-PMI, KNN-CMI): alpha=0.025.
Positive control run on the same 8-state deterministic SPA as parent, same seed, same procedure.
decision_rule:
Verdict priority: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING > MEASUREMENT_INVALID > SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST.

FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING triggers if ANY of:
  (1) C1: All 4 estimators have |shuffled-action null mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000
  (2) C3: Positive control K3 < 1.0 bit OR p > 0.001
  (3) Determinism check fails (any (state,action) has < 2 unique candidates)

MEASUREMENT_INVALID triggers if:
  (4) Fewer than 30% of (state,action) strata have >= 5 records at N=5000
  (5) stratum_size_bias_decomposition has < 2 non-empty size buckets

SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of:
  (C1) At least 1 estimator has |null_mean| < 0.1 bits
  (C3) Positive control passes
  (C6) Determinism check passes
  (C7) >= 2 non-empty size buckets in stratum decomposition

Phase 2 (beyond-Markov, only if SURVIVES on C1):
  (C2) K3 PMI - K2 PMI > 0.1 bits AND bootstrap 95% CI lower > 0.0
  (C4) |K2(N=50000) - K2(N=5000)| <= 0.2 bits for the best estimator
product_consequence_positive: If bias is eliminated (H1 passes): the PMI research program is unblocked. Valid beyond-Markov testing becomes possible on this SPA class. The estimator convergence problem is shown to be environment-caused (deterministic/stochastic mixing), not intrinsic to plug-in estimation. This opens the path to: (a) testing K3-K2 on the stochastic SPA, (b) re-validating prior parent signals (0.933-bit K2 PMI) with proper null centering, (c) eventually testing on production SPAs with stochastic transitions.
product_consequence_negative: If bias persists (H0 confirmed): the plug-in PMI estimator is fundamentally biased for strata-varying-size SPA estimation regardless of determinism ratio. This closes the SPA-redesign pathway and requires truly orthogonal frameworks (KSG CMI, Bayesian model comparison, likelihood-ratio tests, consistently smoothed joint estimators) as the required next attack vector. The bias is intrinsic to the estimation method, not the environment.
estimated_cost: Low-medium. Single Python script execution on 12-state SPA, N=5000 primary + N=50000 convergence test. ~10 minutes compute. 500 shuffled-action permutations. No browser/network required. Uses existing parent run_experiment.py infrastructure with modified CANDIDATES.
expected_information_gain: High. This experiment answers the critical fork question from the parent handoff: is the bias environment-level (fixable by SPA redesign) or estimator-level (requiring orthogonal frameworks)? A definitive answer in either direction closes one pathway and opens the other. The experiment is small but resolves the highest-uncertainty question in the Physics lane's current state.
